title: Pearl Vault — Brushed Gold Consulting Glass
description: Warm pearl-frosted glass cards float over a dim charcoal-teal field, anchored by 0.5–1px champagne-gold hairlines — closer to a Kering strategy memo than a SaaS deck. Serif display type and a deliberately un-icy palette separate this from every other glass template in the category.
philosophy: This template exists for rooms where trust is the product — where tactile warmth signals discretion rather than velocity. It refuses tech-cyan glass, neon glow, and any surface that reads 'fintech startup,' borrowing instead from the visual grammar of print luxury: champagne hairlines, warm pearl frosting, and serif display faces with editorial authority. It is built for senior partners and institutional clients who encounter Hermès press kits and private-bank memoranda as professional reading. Restraint here is not minimalism; it is a statement of earned confidence.
goodFor: Boutique strategy, M&A, or restructuring consulting decks
Private-banking and wealth management client pitches
Luxury brand board presentations and annual review covers
3–6 word serif hero statements with minimal supporting copy
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews requiring high-contrast data grids
Startup or growth-stage pitch decks featuring product UI screenshots
High-energy event marketing or promotional slide sets
Audiences expecting a cool-toned or luminescent aqua-glass aesthetic
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like the inside cover of a private-bank memorandum — warm, unhurried, and self-assured. A pearl-frosted glass panel anchors the left half of the composition, leaving the right field as deliberate, undecorated silence that amplifies rather than wastes space. The display headline commands through scale and serif authority alone, not density; a whisper-thin gold rule beneath it pulls the eye gently downward to the subtitle. Avoid luminescent glow, cool-toned frosting, or restless layering — restraint here is a signal of earned institutional confidence, not absence of intention.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; a pearl-frosted glass panel spans cols 1–7, bleeding flush to the left edge with an 8% top-and-bottom margin on the right side — the remaining cols 8–12 are left as open charcoal-teal ground. Display headline sits in cols 2–7, followed immediately by a single hairline-weight champagne rule that runs the width of the panel, then a two-line subtitle block beneath it. Firm name or deck date is set flush-right at the lower baseline in cols 10–12; no persistent header band exists on this slide.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a leaf from a private-bank strategy memorandum — warm, frosted, and weighted with quiet authority. A dominant pearl-glass card anchors the left-to-center field, holding an editorial headline and restrained body copy; the narrower right column surfaces a single pullout figure or subordinate point, divided by hairline rather than white space alone. Composition is deliberately asymmetric yet settled, with the deep warm ground bleeding fully behind all surfaces. Avoid cool luminescence, neon edge glow, or any uniform modular grid rhythm that would signal tech or fintech origins.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8% outer margin on all sides; a primary pearl-frosted glass card occupies cols 1–8, carrying the section headline and supporting body copy, while cols 9–12 host a narrow accent panel — a single champagne-gold hairline rule divides them vertically rather than a gap. Hierarchy is driven by size contrast plus thin horizontal hairline rules beneath label text, not weight alone. Page number sits bottom-right outside the card boundary. No top header band; the charcoal-teal ground bleeds edge-to-edge behind the floating card system.
